researchDepth: 15-Driver construct review, shared prior-edge consultation, targeted goal/need/motivation landscape and experimental/null source checks. Not a systematic review per Driver; secondary citations do not count as primary extraction.

entityReviews.constructReview: Commitment to a specified behavior, time and context; not performance or intention enactment.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Canonical probability/likelihood and commitment scales may measure different aspects. Retain action/time/referent and distinguish behavioral expectation from resolved intention.
entityReviews.timeReview: Current strength and later stability are different; intention-behavior follow-up is not a direct effect on intention.
entityReviews.unresolved: Eight previously dispositioned incident claims reused; no automatic intention-to-action shortcut.

entityReviews.constructReview: Attachment and determination toward a specified goal; not achieved performance or moral conviction itself.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Five-item commitment measurement work differs from persistence outcomes. Shared action-commitment indicators with PSY-110 can create circular association.
entityReviews.timeReview: Goal attachment can persist while goal remains valued/feasible; no generic permanent change.
entityReviews.unresolved: Exact difficulty/commitment direction requires independent measurement and feasibility; no universal dose-response inferred.

entityReviews.constructReview: Clarity of a goal's target/criterion/endpoint; not difficulty or execution planning.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Externally specifying a target does not prove participant encoded a correspondingly precise internal goal. Coded verbal precision requires fidelity and independent assessment.
entityReviews.timeReview: Assigned instructions precede task, but no automatic later monitoring intensity or persistence.
entityReviews.unresolved: No new effect from goal-setting behavior outcomes alone; action versus represented-goal alignment remains research-needed.

entityReviews.constructReview: Perceived difficulty of attaining the goal, not objective task difficulty or success probability alone.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Canonical target-performance-gap indicator does not replace perceived effort/skill demand. Keep classification unchanged.
entityReviews.timeReview: Perceived feasibility can change after feedback; difficulty-performance studies do not identify difficulty-to-commitment timing.
entityReviews.unresolved: Preserve existing NON_MONOTONIC sign and distinguish task versus goal difficulty; no invented inverted-U parameters.

entityReviews.constructReview: Interference among two or more active personal goals, not one difficult task or generic decision conflict.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Resource conflict versus inherent incompatibility and remembered versus experienced interference require explicit goal pairs; shared item judgments can inflate associations.
entityReviews.timeReview: Dynamic competing priorities differ from static goal-network ratings.
entityReviews.unresolved: Conflict's moderation of intention-behavior is inconsistent; not evidence all intentions decrease.

entityReviews.constructReview: Relative priority among active goals; not goal commitment, normative approval or achieved behavior.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Rank or normalized importance is a representation, not a causal numerical weight. Priority manipulation checks require exact comparison set.
entityReviews.timeReview: A temporary prioritization prompt cannot establish enduring value change.
entityReviews.unresolved: Promising priority experiments concern intention-behavior coupling, not an isolated ordinary edge or exact currently modeled target.

entityReviews.constructReview: Pursuing an activity for inherent interest/enjoyment, not all autonomous reasons or any persistence.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Interest/enjoyment subscale is separated from competence, value, effort and choice subscales. Free-choice time and task output are not identical to the latent construct.
entityReviews.timeReview: Bounded unit-end homework interest does not establish trait change, long-term learning or general work motivation.
entityReviews.unresolved: Retain one bounded homework-interest effect; option-choice null and design/missingness limitations preserved.

entityReviews.constructReview: Self-endorsed regulation consistent with accepted values/goals, which can include non-enjoyable but valued action.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Identified regulation differs from intrinsic interest. Relative autonomy composites can mix facets and should not be interpreted as one manipulated primitive.
entityReviews.timeReview: Momentary volition and internalization over longer periods need separate evidence.
entityReviews.unresolved: Need satisfaction and autonomous regulation share volition wording; meta-analytic path models do not isolate this mediator.

entityReviews.constructReview: Pressure-driven regulation through external demands or internal guilt; not mere reward receipt.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Pressure/tension rating is not itself controlled regulation; external and introjected motives can coexist with autonomous reasons.
entityReviews.timeReview: Short-lived task tension does not show stable extrinsic orientation.
entityReviews.unresolved: Reward contingency reviews differ in tasks, measures and inclusion rules; no universal reward-crowding or controlled-motivation effect.

entityReviews.constructReview: Experienced volition and choice in a context, not objective options, legal autonomy or generic perceived control.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Perceived option availability and freely endorsed action are distinguishable. A manipulation check about options cannot stand in for whole need satisfaction.
entityReviews.timeReview: State experience, not permanent freedom or personality; canonical delay remains unverified narrative.
entityReviews.unresolved: Choice effects on intrinsic interest do not independently establish autonomy as a causal mediator.

entityReviews.constructReview: Experienced effectiveness/capability in valued activities; distinguish prospective self-efficacy from current mastery.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Feeling competent and successful test performance are distinct. Need scales, task-specific competence and capability expectancy require scope matching.
entityReviews.timeReview: Task-level feedback may alter current appraisal without changing skill or enduring competence.
entityReviews.unresolved: Homework competence ratings are promising, but no additional formal effect retained without fuller need/valued-outcome alignment.

entityReviews.constructReview: Feeling cared for, connected and significant to others; not number of ties, support availability or ostracism exposure.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Substantial content overlap with PSY-020 belonging requires contextual referents, not automatic synonymy or causal inverse.
entityReviews.timeReview: A virtual exclusion moment does not establish sustained relatedness need change.
entityReviews.unresolved: Reuse F03 social-exclusion research; no duplicate inverse effect or new social-tie claim.

entityReviews.constructReview: Current motivation toward a desired outcome, not enduring reward sensitivity or every effort choice.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Effort discounting in reward tasks is a partial behavioral operationalization; distinguish cognitive from physical domains and motivational quality.
entityReviews.timeReview: State responsiveness can vary despite stable trait disposition; no state-to-trait conversion.
entityReviews.unresolved: Sleep restriction reduced cognitive effort willingness but not physical willingness; exact broad approach endpoint remains unresolved.

entityReviews.constructReview: Current motivation to avoid/prevent an unwanted state; can coexist with approach motivation.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Avoidance-oriented goal instructions and fear/arousal measures are not interchangeable. Performance-avoidance and mastery/approach contrasts bundle goal content.
entityReviews.timeReview: Immediate threat-driven motivation does not establish trait avoidance.
entityReviews.unresolved: No automatic inverse relationship with approach and no direct effect derived from fear-appeal behavior.

entityReviews.constructReview: Expected regret concerning a specific future action OR omission, not experienced regret after an outcome.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Question wording determines whether more regret predicts less or more intention. Shared self-report and prior preference may explain associations.
entityReviews.timeReview: Prospective prediction does not identify a causal effect of the latent anticipated emotion.
entityReviews.unresolved: Current mechanism already refers to not acting; revision proposal makes that qualification explicit and lowers causal certainty without implementing a change.

existingReviews.rationale: Current volition-to-self-endorsed-regulation mechanism is plausible but overlapping wording and pooled SDT correlations do not isolate independent causal change.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Ng uses meta-analyzed correlations/path analysis; Reeve's option-choice manipulation did not increase volition. Neither proves all need satisfaction causes later regulation.
existingReviews.proposal: Specify independently measured autonomy experience and later regulation, distinguishing internalization from simultaneous shared items and provider support.

existingReviews.rationale: Competence and intrinsic interest are related, but feedback/choice manipulations affect multiple experiences rather than randomizing competence alone.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Positive polarity coexists with legacy inverted-U note; task interest, performance and competence subscales must not be pooled. Correlational mediator path is not identified.
existingReviews.proposal: Restrict to task-specific perceived competence with independent later interest measure and autonomy/challenge conditions; resolve shape/causal-role questions before any replacement.

existingReviews.rationale: A clear goal supplies a comparison criterion, but Harkin experimentally promotes monitoring rather than identifying goal-specificity-to-monitoring intensity.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Specific+difficult goal packages and achieved performance are not isolated specificity or checking frequency; opportunity/feedback availability required.
existingReviews.proposal: Separate clear criterion affordance from actual monitoring frequency; obtain exact manipulation/measurement and timing before a bounded replacement.

existingReviews.rationale: Retain current NON_MONOTONIC context dependence, but review cited evidence for perceived difficulty causing commitment rather than commitment moderating difficulty-to-performance.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Task difficulty is not goal difficulty; performance outcomes and self-efficacy cannot establish an inverted-U commitment response.
existingReviews.proposal: Keep feasibility, acceptance, goal origin and independent commitment measure explicit; no invented threshold or universal positive/negative slope.

existingReviews.rationale: Conflict can weaken one goal, strengthen prioritization of another, or affect enactment without changing intention; exact negative latent-intention effect is unresolved.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Goal-conflict moderation was inconsistent; goal structure, experience and measurement window differ. Do not turn moderation into ordinary causation.

existingReviews.rationale: The current mechanism is already inaction-qualified. Preserve it, but explicit source findings distinguish action versus inaction regret and largely associative evidence.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Action regret predicts weaker intention whereas inaction regret predicts stronger intention. Prediction beyond TPB and prospective association do not identify latent-regret causation.
existingReviews.proposal: Represent inaction regret about specified behavior/outcome and later intention; separate action-regret direction, measurement framing and causal evidence requirements.

existingReviews.rationale: A trait predisposition can affect state response, but scale-development provenance alone does not identify a manipulable independent trait-to-state causal contribution.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Reward sensitivity definition already includes motivational activation; shared BAS/approach indicators, stable-trait versus momentary state and outcome proxies require disentangling.

existingReviews.rationale: Moralized positions can accompany stronger action commitment, but reviewed work concerns attitude conviction and collective participation, not isolated goal attachment.
existingReviews.nullContrary: SRC160 and SRC-501 resolve to the SAME review; no independent replication. PSY-110 action-commitment indicator risks overlap with target.
existingReviews.proposal: Specify moral basis distinct from commitment items, a named compatible goal and temporal ordering; preserve potential inflexibility/harm rather than universal benefit.

hypotheses.question: Intention is equivalent to action.
hypotheses.reason: Commitment and enactment differ; intention-behavior gap is not ontology equivalence.

hypotheses.question: Goal commitment and intention strength overlap.
hypotheses.reason: Goal attachment differs from action/time-specific intention; resolve aligned referents/items before an equivalence claim.

hypotheses.question: Goal performance proves goal commitment increased.
hypotheses.reason: Behavior outcome and measured attachment are not interchangeable.

hypotheses.question: Goal specification changes later self-monitoring.
hypotheses.reason: Existing REL-PSY-021 review reused; no second discovery edge.

hypotheses.question: A harder task proves a harder internal goal caused commitment.
hypotheses.reason: Task difficulty, perceived goal demand and commitment are different; no shortcut from performance.

hypotheses.question: Goal priority modifies intention-to-physical-activity.
hypotheses.reason: Experimental priority studies promising, but exact governed causal edge/behavior endpoint and intervention content require alignment; do not substitute priority→intention.

hypotheses.question: Goal conflict modifies intention-to-action.
hypotheses.reason: Conflicting experimental/observational results; no exact edge-target assertion retained.

hypotheses.question: Autonomous motivation equals intrinsic motivation.
hypotheses.reason: Self-endorsed valued action may not be enjoyable; do not merge.

hypotheses.question: Controlled motivation is simply negative autonomous motivation.
hypotheses.reason: Pressured and self-endorsed reasons can coexist; scale contrast not inverse causal force.

hypotheses.question: Bounded task-option choice can increase homework interest.
hypotheses.reason: Discovery of EA-CAND-PSY-LAYER-0007 only; not another proposition. High-school homework scope, null in other option tasks and missingness retained.

hypotheses.question: Choice→autonomy→intrinsic motivation pathway.
hypotheses.reason: Randomizing choices does not randomize autonomy. Patall Analysis 2 explicitly correlational; Reeve SEM cannot identify transmitted causal effect.

hypotheses.question: Positive competence feedback changes intrinsic interest.
hypotheses.reason: Reward reviews separate verbal feedback/tangible contingencies, but exact feedback identity, task and competence-independent effect scope need primary alignment.

hypotheses.question: Rewards universally destroy intrinsic motivation.
hypotheses.reason: Contingency, prior task interest, age and self-report versus behavioral measures differ; competing syntheses overlap.

hypotheses.question: Perceived option availability is identical to autonomy satisfaction.
hypotheses.reason: Option manipulation may change perceived choice without volition or intrinsic interest.

hypotheses.question: Relatedness satisfaction and belonging are synonymous.
hypotheses.reason: Overlapping experience but distinct referent/need formulation; consult F03, no new semantic equality.

hypotheses.question: Competence satisfaction and self-efficacy are equivalent.
hypotheses.reason: Current effectiveness and prospective capability differ; shared capable wording can cause measurement overlap.

hypotheses.question: Sleep restriction lowers approach motivation.
hypotheses.reason: Cognitive reward-effort willingness decreased but physical willingness did not; effort valuation endpoint differs from general approach motivation. Consult F10 without starting external Family work.

hypotheses.question: Sleep-loss state effects permanently alter reward sensitivity.
hypotheses.reason: No enduring trait evidence; do not infer PSY-F14 trait change.

hypotheses.question: Natural-environment exposure increases intrinsic motivation.
hypotheses.reason: Intrinsic aspirations in nature studies are goal contents/values, not enjoyment of a task; do not rename the endpoint.

hypotheses.question: Gamification increases autonomous or intrinsic motivation.
hypotheses.reason: Configurations and motivational outcome composites differ; higher-rigor subsplit effects less stable. No component efficacy or single generic gamification identity.

hypotheses.question: Cultural interdependence changes effects of personal choice.
hypotheses.reason: Choice review discusses culture/referent heterogeneity; country/ethnic group is not an exact moderator Driver or randomized culture.

hypotheses.question: Institutional autonomy-support rules increase autonomy need satisfaction.
hypotheses.reason: Rule occurrence/availability, experienced support and volition are separate; health correlational paths do not identify rule efficacy.

hypotheses.question: Social connection changes relatedness satisfaction.
hypotheses.reason: Earlier F03 exclusion/belonging review supplies constraints; no independent inverse contribution inferred.

hypotheses.question: Anticipated regret always increases intention.
hypotheses.reason: Action and inaction regret have opposite associations; current inaction mechanism must not be generalized.

hypotheses.question: Regret prompts alter anticipated regret and intention.
hypotheses.reason: Question salience and latent emotion are not equivalent; paired action/inaction wording and manipulation checks required.

hypotheses.question: Mastery versus performance instructions change intrinsic interest.
hypotheses.reason: Experimental synthesis indicates feedback and approach/avoidance contingency; exact goal orientation is not identical to general PSY-038/039.

hypotheses.question: Relative priority score is an executable causal weight.
hypotheses.reason: Rank/normalization describes priority only; no quantitative execution contract.

hypotheses.question: External shock or routine demand changes goal priority/conflict.
hypotheses.reason: Plausible resource/opportunity mechanism but no exact natural-experiment endpoint extraction in this bounded search; occurrence alone not consequence.

canonicalSourceReviews.finding: Goal-setting retrospective distinguishes task difficulty, goal difficulty, performance and commitment; specific-plus-difficult interventions do not isolate every endpoint.
184 datasets and meta-analyzed correlation/path models; need/regulation/health associations not independently identified mediators.
138 randomized monitoring interventions assess monitoring and attainment, not isolated specificity→monitoring. Mediation wording not proof of transmitted pathway.
81 studies; action regret predicts less intention, inaction regret more; association synthesis, no universal sign.
Augmented TPB predictions remain predictions; overlap with later regret review possible, not independent replication.
Carver/White title and authors verified via publisher DOI metadata; original construct-specific causal findings not extracted here.
Publisher-deposited abstract distinguishes moral conviction and attitude strength; social/political consequences are not exact goal-commitment manipulation.
Same DOI/work as SRC-501; 16 reviews/meta-analyses of collective behavior, not moral-conviction→goal-attachment identification.
Same da Costa et al. 2023 review as SRC160. Stored Zumeta attribution inconsistent with verified authors; preserve canonical unchanged and flag.
129 independent studies/138 samples mainly moderate quality on intention-physical-activity coupling, not deterministic enactment.
Ryan/Deci 2000 PubMed 11392867 abstract verified; need-support integrative synthesis, not proof of independent causal segments.
F01/F02/F03 experimental TPB alignment and manipulation bundles retained.
Cane et al. Theoretical Domains Framework validation, NOT a goal-conflict or self-regulation causal experiment. Canonical record unchanged.
Foundational self-efficacy source identity resolves, but no abstract returned; not scored as an exact causal finding.
F02 Rogers DOI/source-alignment issue retained; no canonical correction.
F03 belonging/need boundary review reused, no duplicate exclusion effect.
F03 Cyberball outcome/measurement caveats reused; broad pooled outcomes are not independent relatedness manipulation.
Lerner et al. 2015 emotion/decision review notes beneficial and harmful effects, not a direct specific anticipated-regret effect.

queries: Registered Ng/Harkin/Brewer/Sandberg/Rhodes abstracts and Locke/Latham selected text; Carver/White and Skitka publisher metadata; da Costa duplicate reconciliation
searchLog.depth: Production endpoints/aliases reviewed first; 8 shared existing reviews reused, 8 newly owned reviews assessed. Primary abstracts and selected source sections, not fourteen isolated bibliographies.

queries: Patall Cooper Robinson 2008 effects choice intrinsic motivation meta-analysis
Goal commitment measurement Klein 1999 2001; unique goal setting Epton 2017
Goal priority conflict intention-health-behavior Conner 2016; Gorges Grund conceptual review
searchLog.depth: Meta-analysis and original-study abstracts plus measurement distinctions; moderation/behavior outcomes not converted to ordinary causal edges.

queries: Patall Cooper Wynn 2010 homework choice interest/enjoyment methods missing data crossover
Reeve Nix Hamm 2003 option versus action choice null
Deci Koestner Ryan 1999 versus Cameron Banko Pierce 2001 rewards
searchLog.depth: Primary homework and puzzle papers selected methods/results/limitations; reward syntheses abstracts. Source findings authored before synthesis; no generic rewards or choice efficacy.

queries: Sleep restriction cognitive not physical motivation Jurgelis 2022
Nature immersion intrinsic aspirations Weinstein Przybylski Ryan 2009
Gamification learning Sailer Homner 2020 motivational outcomes methodological rigor
searchLog.depth: Primary abstracts/publisher material screened. Nature aspiration, effort valuation and broad gamification outcomes not re-labeled exact intrinsic motivation. All eight origin Layers and nine domains considered; unsupported cells remain uninvestigated/insufficient.

queries: Option choice null, homework missingness, same-sample correlational Analysis 2, reward-review disagreements
Anticipated regret action versus inaction; priority/conflict inconsistent moderation; duplicated SRC160/SRC-501
searchLog.depth: Re-read selected experimental methods/null discussion and original meta-analysis abstracts. No mediation from SEM; no unsupported null; no false independent replication. Crossref throttled once on Sailer; used authoritative publisher bibliography already read, not stale response.
